Tungod kay duha ang atong mata, mas sayon natong matantya kung unsa kalayo ang usa ka butang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Eyelashes and eyebrows are hairs whose job is to shield your eyes from dust and sweat.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes human eyelashes and eyebrows as hairs that protect the eyes from dust and sweat. G3-L-4 requires observing and describing outer body parts of animals and identifying their role in movement and gathering food. The card shares the broad topic of body parts but does not address animal body parts or the roles of moving and gathering food, so it is only related.

copy.en: Eyelashes and eyebrows are hairs whose job is to shield your eyes from dust and sweat.
copy.tl: Ang pilikmata at kilay ay buhok na nagpoprotekta sa iyong mata laban sa alikabok at pawis.
copy.bis: Ang pilok ug kilay mga buhok nga manalipod sa imong mata batok sa abog ug singot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Having two forward-facing eyes gives us depth perception!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes eyes as an outer body part, but the competency focuses on identifying the role of outer body parts (head, legs, wings) in movement and gathering food. Depth perception is not related to moving or gathering food, so the card does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Having two forward-facing eyes gives us depth perception! Our brain compares the slightly different images from each eye to judge distance.
copy.tl: Ang pagkakaroon ng dalawang forward-facing eyes ay nagbibigay sa atin ng depth perception! Inihahambing ng utak ang bahagyang magkaibang imahe mula sa bawat mata para malaman ang distansya.
copy.bis: Ang pagkaon og duha ka forward-facing eyes nagahatag sa ato og depth perception! Ang utok nagatandi sa bahay-bahay nga lain-laing hulagway gikan sa matag mata aron mahibaw-an ang gilay-on.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Another temperature scale called Fahrenheit is used to measure heat in some countries, like the United States!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and appropriately use units in simple science activities, such as milligrams (mg), grams (g), kilograms (kg), and degrees centigrade (C)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions Fahrenheit, a temperature unit, but the competency specifically requires identifying and using units such as milligrams, grams, kilograms, and degrees centigrade (Celsius). The card does not teach how to identify or use these units in simple science activities; it only states that Fahrenheit is used in some countries. This is related to temperature units but does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Another temperature scale called Fahrenheit is used to measure heat in some countries, like the United States!
copy.tl: May ibang iskala ng temperatura na tinatawag na Fahrenheit na ginagamit sa ilang bansa gaya ng Estados Unidos!
copy.bis: Adunay laing iskala sa temperatura nga gitawag Fahrenheit nga gigamit sa ubang nasud sama sa Estados Unidos!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fish breathe using gills, not lungs — water passes through the gills, which take in oxygen dissolved in the water!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes gills as a fish body part used for breathing, but G3-L-4 specifically targets outer body parts (head, legs, wings) and their role in movement and food gathering. Gills are not presented in that context, so the card only shares the broad topic of animal body parts without directly supporting the competency's skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fish breathe using gills, not lungs — water passes through the gills, which take in oxygen dissolved in the water!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: G5-L-2 requires identifying the human respiratory system parts (nose, windpipe, lungs) from pictures/diagrams and describing how they work. The card discusses fish gills and explicitly contrasts them with lungs, but does not teach the human respiratory system parts or their function. It is only tangentially related through the concept of breathing.

copy.en:
How do fish breathe underwater?

Fish breathe using gills, not lungs — water passes through the gills, which take in oxygen dissolved in the water!
copy.tl:
Paano humihinga ang isda sa tubig?

Humihinga ang isda gamit ang hasang (gills), hindi baga — dumadaan ang tubig sa hasang at kinukuha nito ang oxygen na natunaw sa tubig!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pag-ginhawa sa isda ilawom sa tubig?

Moginhawa ang isda gamit ang hasang (gills), dili baga — moagi ang tubig sa hasang ug kuhaon niini ang oxygen nga natunaw sa tubig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A rock sinks because it has higher density than water!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses density, which is a physical property, but the competency specifically targets properties like hard, shiny, or stretchable. Density is not one of the listed examples and the card does not describe those properties, so it only shares the broad subject of physical properties.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: That means the rock is heavier than the same amount of water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies mass and volume through density, but it does not explicitly describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space. The focus is on sinking due to density, not on the fundamental definition of matter, so it provides only related background.

copy.en: A rock sinks because it has higher density than water! That means the rock is heavier than the same amount of water, so it drops straight down.
copy.tl: Lumulubog ang bato dahil mas mataas ang density nito kaysa tubig! Ibig sabihin, mas mabigat ang bato kaysa katumbas nitong dami ng tubig, kaya bumababa ito pababa.
copy.bis: Molunod ang bato kay mas taas ang density niini kaysa tubig! Pasabot niini, mas bug-at ang bato kaysa katumbas niini nga gidaghanon sa tubig, mao nga mokanaog kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When something vibrates quickly, it makes a high-pitched sound!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: research using secondary sources to identify how the properties of waves are described using scientific terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, and velocity
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a basic relationship between vibration speed and pitch, which relates to frequency, but it does not involve researching secondary sources or identifying how wave properties (amplitude, frequency, wavelength, velocity) are described. It provides no direct instructional support for the competency's research and terminology focus.

copy.en:
What happens when something vibrates really fast?

When something vibrates quickly, it makes a high-pitched sound!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari kapag mabilis ang yanig?

Kapag mabilis ang yanig ng isang bagay, mataas ang pitch ng tunog na nalilikha nito!
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo kon paspas magkurog ang usa ka butang?

Kon paspas magkurog ang usa ka butang, taas ang pitch sa tingog nga mahimo niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A machine called a centrifuge spins blood very fast!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe examples of accelerating objects at school and in the local community, including objects that show uniform circular motion
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a centrifuge spinning very fast, which is an example of circular motion, but it does not describe acceleration, uniform circular motion, or how to observe/describe accelerating objects. The focus is blood separation, not the physics of acceleration.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The heavier parts settle at the bottom, while the lighter parts stay on top.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions heavier and lighter parts separating, touching on heaviness, but it does not explore or describe how size, shape, heaviness, material, or surface texture affect the movement of objects. The separation is due to spinning, not a study of factors affecting movement.

copy.en:
How do hospitals separate the parts of blood so quickly?

A machine called a centrifuge spins blood very fast! The heavier parts settle at the bottom, while the lighter parts stay on top.
copy.tl:
Paano mabilis na ihihiwalay ng mga ospital ang mga bahagi ng dugo?

May makinang tinatawag na centrifuge na umiikot nang sobrang bilis! Ang mas mabibigat na bahagi ay napupunta sa ilalim, at ang magagaan sa itaas.
copy.bis:
Unsaon paspas nga pagbulag sa mga ospital sa mga bahin sa dugo?

Adunay makina nga gitawag og centrifuge nga motuyok og paspas kaayo! Ang mas bug-at nga bahin moadto sa ilawom, ug ang gaan sa ibabaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A washing machine spins fast to squeeze water out!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe examples of accelerating objects at school and in the local community, including objects that show uniform circular motion
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an everyday example of spinning, but it does not describe acceleration or uniform circular motion, nor does it ask students to observe or describe such motion. It only mentions that the machine spins fast and flings water, which is background context rather than direct support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A washing machine spins fast to squeeze water out!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify inertia as the tendency for an object to stay at rest or in motion unless acted on by an unbalanced net force
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions spinning and speed but does not discuss inertia, rest, motion, or unbalanced net force. It provides no instructional support for identifying inertia as the tendency to stay at rest or in motion unless acted on by an unbalanced net force.

copy.en: A washing machine spins fast to squeeze water out! The speed flings water through tiny drum holes, so clothes come out partly dry.
copy.tl: Mabilis na umiikot ang washing machine para alisin ang tubig! Ang bilis ay tumitilapon ng tubig sa maliliit na butas, kaya bahagyang tuyo na ang damit.
copy.bis: Paspas nga motuyok ang washing machine aron makuha ang tubig! Ang katulin molabay og tubig sa gagmay nga lungag, mao nga mamala-mala ang sinina.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: reached almost 44 kilometers per hour in a short sprint
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a speed value (44 km/h) for Usain Bolt but does not explain that speed is how far an object moves in a given time. It provides an example of speed without teaching the definition or relationship between distance and time, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: The fastest human, like Usain Bolt, reached almost 44 kilometers per hour in a short sprint!
copy.tl: Ang pinakamabilis na tao, tulad ni Usain Bolt, ay umabot ng halos 44 kilometro kada oras sa maikling takbo!
copy.bis: Ang pinakapaspas nga tawo, sama ni Usain Bolt, nakakab-ot og duol sa 44 ka kilometro kada oras sa mubo nga dagan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the fastest runner of all the land animals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that the cheetah is the fastest land animal. It does not define speed as distance over time, nor does it provide any information about measuring distance and time. This is a factual example of speed but does not directly teach the competency's concept.

copy.en:
What's the fastest land animal?

The cheetah — it is the fastest runner of all the land animals.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamabilis na hayop sa lupa?

Ang cheetah — ito ang pinakamabilis tumakbo sa lahat ng hayop sa lupa.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakapaspas nga hayop sa yuta?

Ang cheetah — kini ang pinakapaspas modagan sa tanang hayop sa yuta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The ostrich is the fastest running bird
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about an ostrich being a fast bird but does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups. It only mentions a bird, which is one of the animal groups, but provides no classification instruction or content.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: reaching speeds of about 70 km/h
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a speed value but does not define speed as distance over time. It does not teach the concept that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed; it merely gives a speed figure for an ostrich.

copy.en:
What is the fastest running bird?

The ostrich is the fastest running bird, reaching speeds of about 70 km/h (around 43 mph)!
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamabilis na tumatakbong ibon?

Ang ostrich ang pinakamabilis tumakbo sa lahat ng ibon, umaabot ng mga 70 km/h (mga 43 mph)!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakapaspas nga langgam modagan?

Ang ostrich ang pinakapaspas nga langgam modagan, makaabot ug mga 70 km/h (mga 43 mph)!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Healthy fats like omega-3 from fish help your brain grow and keep your cells strong.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses healthy fats and omega-3 for brain and cell health, but does not identify basic needs of living things such as air, food, water, and shelter. Food is only implied as a general topic, not taught as a basic need.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: keep your cells strong
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions cells only in the context of health benefits of omega-3. It does not address unicellular versus multicellular organisms, which is the core of the competency.

copy.en:
Is all fat bad for you?

Not all fat is bad! Healthy fats like omega-3 from fish help your brain grow and keep your cells strong.
copy.tl:
Masama ba lahat ng taba?

Hindi pala lahat ng taba masama! Ang malusog na taba gaya ng omega-3 mula sa isda ay tumutulong sa pag-unlad ng utak at pader ng selula.
copy.bis:
Dautan ba tanang taba?

Dili diay tanang taba dautan! Ang maayong taba sama sa omega-3 gikan sa isda motabang sa pag-uswag sa utok ug istruktura sa cell.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fats from oil, nuts, and some meats store energy and help your body absorb certain vitamins
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses fats as a nutrient and vitamin absorption, but does not describe how any of the listed body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) work. It is only tangentially related to the digestive system.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fats from oil, nuts, and some meats store energy and help your body absorb certain vitamins
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a food type (fats) but does not identify basic needs of living things such as air, food, water, and shelter. It does not directly support the competency's focus on identifying basic needs.

copy.en: Fats from oil, nuts, and some meats store energy and help your body absorb certain vitamins — but too much isn't healthy.
copy.tl: Ang taba mula sa mantika, mani, at ilang karne ay nag-iimbak ng enerhiya at tumutulong sa katawan na sumipsip ng bitamina, pero hindi mabuti ang sobra.
copy.bis: Ang tambok gikan sa lana, mani, ug pipila ka karne nagtipig og kusog ug motabang sa lawas nga makasuyop og bitamina, apan dili maayo ang sobra.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water rolls right off a bird's smooth feathers
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions feathers, an outer body part of an animal, but the competency requires identifying the role of outer body parts such as head, legs, or wings in moving and gathering food. The card instead describes feathers keeping the bird dry, which does not support the stated skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water rolls right off a bird's smooth feathers
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes water rolling off feathers, not the physical properties of solid materials such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. Feathers are not presented as solid materials with described physical properties, so it does not directly support this competency.

copy.en: Water rolls right off a bird's smooth feathers, so it stays dry even when it's raining.
copy.tl: Tumutulo lang ang tubig sa makinis na balahibo ng ibon kaya nananatili itong tuyo kahit umuulan.
copy.bis: Ang tubig modahili ra sa hapsay nga balhibo sa langgam busa magpabilin kining uga bisan og nag-ulan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: most common mineral group in Earth's crust
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to name and describe the upper crustal layers of the solid earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies feldspar as the most common mineral group in the crust, but the competency requires naming and describing the upper crustal layers of the solid earth. Mineral composition is not the same as crustal layers; the card does not address layers or their description.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: most common mineral group in Earth's crust
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The competency involves observing/collecting rocks and describing their features (texture, color, grain crystal size). The card only states that feldspar is the most common mineral group; it does not support rock observation, collection, or feature comparison.

copy.en:
What is the most common mineral group in Earth's crust?

It's feldspar! This mineral group is the most common one found in the Earth's crust — it's everywhere!
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakakaraniwang grupo ng mineral sa crust ng Earth?

Feldspar ito! Ang grupong ito ng mineral ang pinakakaraniwan sa crust ng Earth — nasa lahat ng lugar ito!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakakomon nga grupo sa mineral sa crust sa Yuta?

Feldspar kini! Kini nga grupo sa mineral mao ang pinakakomon nga makita sa crust sa Yuta — naa kini bisan asa!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the pickling keeps it fresh
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions as applied in food preservation and materials production, control of fire, pollution, and corrosion
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions food preservation (pickling keeps it fresh) but does not explain any factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions, such as temperature, concentration, or surface area. It only states a fact about pickling without addressing the competency's core skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the pickling keeps it fresh
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate ways to minimize harmful changes in materials, such as restriction of burning of waste materials, and care in handling reactive materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a preservation method but does not demonstrate ways to minimize harmful changes in materials, such as restricting burning or handling reactive materials. It does not teach the competency's action.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: made of pickled green papaya with vinegar, sugar, and salt
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in solid materials make them useful, such as when they are shaped, pressed, hammered, joined, or cut
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a change in a material (pickling) but does not describe how changes in solid materials make them useful through shaping, pressing, hammering, joining, or cutting. The pickling process is not one of the listed changes and the card does not explain usefulness in the required way.

copy.en: Atchara is a Filipino favorite made of pickled green papaya with vinegar, sugar, and salt — the pickling keeps it fresh and gives it a tangy taste.
copy.tl: Ang atchara ay tradisyonal na Pinoy na pickled na hilaw na papaya na ginagawa gamit ang suka, asukal, at asin — nagbibigay ito ng maasim na lasa at pinapanatiling sariwa ang papaya.
copy.bis: Ang atchara usa ka tradisyonal nga Pinoy nga pickled nga hilaw nga papaya nga hinimo gamit ang suka, asukal, ug asin — nagpreserba kini sa papaya ug naghatag og maasim nga lasa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Those bubbles are just carbon dioxide made by helpful microbes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify the products of traditional biotechnology through fermentation (e.g. cheese, soy sauce, vinegar, nata de coco)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses fermentation and carbon dioxide production but does not identify any traditional biotechnology products such as cheese, soy sauce, vinegar, or nata de coco. It only addresses a misconception about bubbles, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Those bubbles are just carbon dioxide
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions carbon dioxide, which is a gas, but it does not teach the three states of matter (solids, liquids, gases) or their identification. The mention is incidental and does not support the competency's skill.

copy.en:
Do bubbles mean fermented food is spoiled?

No! Those bubbles are just carbon dioxide made by helpful microbes — actually a sign that the fermentation is working properly.
copy.tl:
Nangangahulugan ba ng sira ang mga bula sa fermented na pagkain?

Hindi! Ang mga bulang iyon ay carbon dioxide lang na inilalabas ng mabubuting mikrobyo — tanda pa nga na maayos ang proseso.
copy.bis:
Nagpasabot ba og daot ang bula sa fermented nga pagkaon?

Dili! Kadtong mga bula kay carbon dioxide ra nga gibuga sa mapuslanong mikrobyo — timaan gani nga maayo ang proseso.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's called a frond — it has a stalk with many small leaflets lined up on both sides.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the structure of a fern frond (leaf) but does not address the role of plant parts (leaves, roots, stems) in getting water and nutrients from the soil, which is the focus of G3-L-5.

copy.en:
What is a whole fern leaf called?

It's called a frond — it has a stalk with many small leaflets lined up on both sides.
copy.tl:
Ano ang tawag sa buong dahon ng pako?

Frond ang tawag dito — may tangkay ito at maraming maliliit na dahon-dahon na nakahanay sa magkabilang gilid.
copy.bis:
Unsay tawag sa tibuok dahon sa pako?

Frond ang tawag — naa kini punoan ug daghang gagmay nga dahon nga nagsunod-sunod sa duha ka kilid.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ferns have tiny tubes that carry water through their whole body
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how plant organs (leaf, stem, roots) work together as the transport system
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water-carrying tubes in ferns but does not describe how leaf, stem, and roots work together as a transport system. It only provides a general fact about vascular tissue, not the organ-level coordination required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ferns have tiny tubes that carry water through their whole body
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not ask students to observe outer parts of plants (leaves, roots, stems) or identify their roles in getting water and nutrients. It only states that ferns have internal tubes for water transport, which is not the same as observing and describing outer plant parts.

copy.en:
Why can ferns grow taller than moss?

Ferns have tiny tubes that carry water through their whole body — that's why they can grow taller than moss, which has no such tubes.
copy.tl:
Bakit mas matangkad ang pako kaysa sa lumot?

May mga maliliit na tubo ang pako na nagdadala ng tubig sa buong katawan nito, kaya mas matangkad itong tumubo kumpara sa lumot na walang ganoong tubo.
copy.bis:
Nganong mas habog motubo ang pako kaysa sa lumot?

Ang pako adunay gagmayng tubo nga nagdala og tubig sa tibuok niyang lawas, mao nga mas habog kini motubo kumpara sa lumot nga walay ingon nga tubo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Thick blankets trap heat inside a feverish body.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses body temperature in the context of fever management, but does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems or its indicators. It only touches on body temperature as a factor, without explaining the concept of homeostasis.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Thick blankets trap heat inside a feverish body.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the difference between heat and temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions heat being trapped and escaping, but does not explain the difference between heat and temperature. It does not define either concept or contrast them, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Should a feverish child wear thick blankets?

No! Thick blankets trap heat inside a feverish body. Light clothing is better so the extra heat can escape.
copy.tl:
Dapat bang balutin ng makapal na kumot ang batang may lagnat?

Hindi! Napipreso ng makapal na kumot ang init sa loob ng katawang may lagnat. Mas mabuti ang magaan na damit para makalabas ang sobrang init.
copy.bis:
Angay ba nga putoson og baga nga habol ang batang hilanaton?

Dili! Ang baga nga habol nagpugong sa kainit sulod sa lawas nga hilanaton. Mas maayo ang magaan nga sinina aron makagawas ang sobra nga kainit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A brain part called the hypothalamus works like a thermostat, setting how warm your body should be.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions body temperature, which is one indicator of homeostasis, but it does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems or explain the concept of homeostasis. It only gives a specific fact about the hypothalamus's role in temperature setting, which is related but not direct support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A brain part called the hypothalamus works like a thermostat, setting how warm your body should be.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how homeostasis is maintained through various feedback mechanisms, both positive and negative
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the hypothalamus as a thermostat for body temperature, which is a component of a feedback mechanism, but it does not explain how homeostasis is maintained through positive or negative feedback mechanisms. It lacks the explanatory content required by the competency.

copy.en:
Which brain part acts like a thermostat?

A brain part called the hypothalamus works like a thermostat, setting how warm your body should be.
copy.tl:
Anong parte ng utak ang parang termostat?

May bahagi ng utak na tinatawag na hypothalamus na parang termostat — ito ang nagtatakda kung gaano dapat kainit ang iyong katawan.
copy.bis:
Unsang bahin sa utok ang morag termostat?

Adunay bahin sa utok nga gitawag og hypothalamus nga sama sa termostat — kini ang nagbutang kon unsa ka init angay ang imong lawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the body lowers the heat it raised once it wins the fight
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure

Living things are commonly sorted into 5 kingdoms: Animalia, Plantae, Fungi, Protista, and Monera.

Ang gabon usa ka panganod nga naporma sa yuta, mao nga morag naglakaw ka sulod sa panganod!
